run.change_description:
Fixed issue of Datepicker displaying the wrong date for users in UTC+ timezones.

Removed usage of var keyword.  Replaced with const.

Removed .idea/vcs.xml.

Made a shell for the integration test for DatePicker displayed/selected dates.

update tests

summary.intent: Fix DatePicker showing a date one day before the user's selection, reported for UTC+ (eastern) timezones in bokeh/bokeh#9129, by compensating for the browser's timezone offset in `DatePickerView._unlocal_date`, and add an integration test shell for the widget.
summary.issue_fit: Met for the reported case: for UTC+ timezones the on_select round trip through `toDateString()` now reproduces the selected day. But the same unconditional offset compensation is also applied to `defaultDate`/`minDate`/`maxDate`, whose values arrive from Python as true UTC-midnight epoch timestamps; for any negative-UTC-offset browser (most of the Americas) this rolls those dates back one day, reintroducing the same class of bug for the opposite hemisphere (see finding bokehjs/date-picker-unlocal-date-negative-offset).
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff reviewed (2/2 changed files). Traced `_unlocal_date` and its three call sites against Bokeh's Python-side datetime serialization (`bokeh/util/serialization.py:convert_datetime_type`) at head; independently reproduced the regression and the intended eastern-timezone fix with scratch Node scripts run under several `TZ` values (Europe/Paris, America/New_York, Pacific/Kiritimati) outside the clone, per the run's execution allowance. The added Selenium/pytest integration tests were inspected by tracing setup through assertions; they were not executed (browser and the project's own build/test runner are unavailable in this environment) — no test in the file exercises the initial displayed date or the min/max bounds, so none would have caught the regression either way. One verification batch confirmed the finding; no follow-up was needed.

findings.title: _unlocal_date shifts epoch-based dates back a day for negative-UTC-offset users
findings.trigger: Triggers when a DatePicker's `value`, `min_date`, or `max_date` is set from the Python/server side (e.g. `DatePicker(value=datetime.date(2019, 9, 20))`) and rendered in a browser whose local timezone has a negative UTC offset (any zone in the Americas, e.g. America/New_York at UTC-4 in September).
findings.impact: Bokeh serializes a Python `date`/`datetime` to milliseconds since the UTC epoch representing true UTC midnight of that date (`bokeh/util/serialization.py` `convert_datetime_type`). `_unlocal_date` now unconditionally subtracts `date.getTimezoneOffset() * 60000` from that instant; for a negative offset this is a positive subtraction that rolls a true UTC-midnight timestamp back into the previous UTC calendar day before `toISOString().substr(0,10)` reads it. The widget then displays the wrong initial date and enforces min/max navigation bounds shifted one day earlier than configured, for the whole lifetime of the widget (`min_date`/`max_date` are re-read from the model on every `render()`). This reintroduces the exact class of defect bokeh/bokeh#9129 reports, just for the opposite hemisphere of timezones — confirmed by reproducing both the merge-base and head behavior for the same UTC-midnight input under `TZ=America/New_York`: head returns `Thu Sep 19 2019`, merge-base correctly returns `Fri Sep 20 2019`.
findings.change: Do not apply the `getTimezoneOffset()` compensation to inputs that are already true UTC-midnight epoch timestamps (the initial `value`, `min_date`, `max_date`); only the client-only round trip through `_on_select`'s `date.toDateString()` needs it, or compute the compensation so it is a no-op for genuine UTC-midnight inputs.

requirements.evidence: Reported repro: selecting a date in a UTC+ timezone (e.g. France, UTC+2) displayed the day before. Traced `_on_select` -> `model.value = date.toDateString()` -> re-render -> `_unlocal_date(new Date(this.model.value))`: `new Date("<toDateString output>")` parses as local midnight, so under the old code `toISOString()` rolled it back a UTC day for eastern timezones. The new offset compensation added at date_picker.ts:82-83 corrects exactly this path; reproduced with a scratch script under TZ=Europe/Paris showing day 20 (correct) where the pre-change code showed day 19.

requirements.source: commit-472e477/"Fixed issue of Datepicker displaying the wrong date for users in UTC+ timezones."
requirements.evidence: The commit's own claim is scoped to UTC+ timezones and is met for that scope (see requirement row above); it makes no claim about UTC- timezones, so the negative-offset regression is an independently admitted defect (finding bokehjs/date-picker-unlocal-date-negative-offset) rather than a contradiction of this stated scope.
